title: One-way bound implies deterministic bound for Boolean functions
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be the input types of Alice and Bob, and let $f : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a two-party Boolean-valued function. If the one-way deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n$ for some $n \in \bbn$, then the (interactive) deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n + 1$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → Bool is a Boolean-valued two-argument function
one-way deterministic communication complexity of f is ≤ n
replaced:
For a Boolean function $f : X \to Y \to \mathtt{Bool}$, if the one-way complexity of $f$
is at most $n$, then the deterministic complexity of $f$ is at most $n + 1$; this
specializes the general bound using $\lceil \log_2 |\mathtt{Bool}| \rceil = 1$.
